extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It comprises 11.5K multimodal questions across six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering), spanning 30 subjects and 183 subfields, with 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection took place in three stages: first, selecting 30 subjects from common university majors across six disciplines where visual inputs provide valuable information; second, recruiting a team of over 50 college students (including coauthors) specializing in these majors to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions where necessary; and third, data cleaning and categorization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed: first, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify and eliminate potential duplicate problems via author review; second, problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format; third, problems were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators manually collected multimodal questions consisting of multiple-choice and open-ended formats, annotating fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty level, and explanations where available. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright/license regulations, avoid sites prohibiting copying, and select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicate problems were reviewed by authors. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence, with regular audits of random samples and team meetings to resolve ambiguities collaboratively.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including coauthors) specializing in corresponding majors across various disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A live-updating leaderboard is maintained at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard, with version tracking documented in a version change log.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Addresses the societal and intellectual need to monitor progress towards Level 3 'Expert AGI', which marks the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor in many industries, carrying risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as there lacks a direct mapping between benchmark performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI must tackle. Additionally, the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal foundation models, large multimodal models (LMMs), and text-only large language models (LLMs) on multi-discipline multimodal perception and reasoning.
